reference.title: Band pull through
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace as the hips go back, breathe out as you drive the hips forward to stand tall.

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: step farther from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, a longer squeeze at the top, then a cable pull-through or a kettlebell swing

cues.text: Stand facing away from the anchor, band tied low behind you and running between the legs. Feet wider than the hips, toes slightly out, both hands on the band in front of the hips, arms long.
Breathe in, soften the knees and push the hips back; let the band draw the hands back between the thighs. Flat back, long arms.
Stop when the hamstrings are stretched and the trunk is well inclined; back still flat.
Breathe out and drive the hips forward to stand tall; the arms just hang on to the band.
Squeeze the glutes at the top without leaning back.

mistakes.fix: Hips go back, shins stay nearly vertical, knees only soft.
Arms are just hooks; the hips do the work.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range and keep the chest proud.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back or arching at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish tall with the ribs down and the glutes squeezed.

kinematics.norm: Hinge with a flat back to a hamstring stretch, as in other hip-hinge exercises (McAllister 2014 compared hinge exercises; clinical opinion for the band version)
Arms long, hands travel back between the thighs and return to the front of the hips (clinical opinion)
Wider than the hips so the band runs between the legs (clinical opinion)
Controlled hinge, forceful hip drive (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band pull through, video (movement reference)
McAllister, Hammond, Schilling, Ferreria, Reed & Weiss 2014, muscle activation during various hamstring exercises (J Strength Cond Res 28(6):1573-1580)
McGill & Marshall 2012, kettlebell swing, snatch, and bottoms-up carry: back and hip muscle activation, motion, and low back loads (J Strength Cond Res)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: a band that slips or snaps can whip forward between the legs.
Keep the back flat; stop the hinge before the low back rounds.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: shorter range, more knee bend.
Hamstring tightness: hinge only as far as the back stays flat.
regressions: Lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.
Hip hinge with a dowel along the back.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Prime mover: hip extension from the hinge to standing tall, hardest near lockout where the band is most stretched (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Prime mover: hip extension from the hinge to standing tall (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Extend the hip with the glutes and lengthen at the bottom of the hinge (hinge exercises load the hamstrings, McAllister 2014).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Extend the hip with the glutes and lengthen at the bottom of the hinge (McAllister 2014).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip in the wide stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip in the wide stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat through the hinge (clinical opinion; back extensors work isometrically in hinge patterns, McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat through the hinge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the ribs stay down at lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the arms close to the body (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the arms close to the body (clinical opinion).
